audit_status.source_base: Greek 1 Corinthians text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for prophecy/tongues, building the assembly, intelligibility, order, women silence textual/pastoral complexity, all things decently/orderly.

verses.restored: Pursue love, and desire spiritual things/gifts, especially that you may prophesy.

familiar.text: Follow after charity, and desire spiritual gifts, but rather that ye may prophesy.

verses.restored: For the one speaking in a tongue does not speak to humans but to the Divine; for no one hears/understands, but in Spirit one speaks mysteries.

familiar.text: For he that speaketh in an unknown tongue speaketh not unto men, but unto God: for no man understandeth him; howbeit in the spirit he speaketh mysteries.

verses.restored: But the one prophesying speaks to humans building up, encouragement, and consolation.

familiar.text: But he that prophesieth speaketh unto men to edification, and exhortation, and comfort.

verses.restored: The one speaking in a tongue builds oneself, but the one prophesying builds the assembly.

familiar.text: He that speaketh in an unknown tongue edifieth himself; but he that prophesieth edifieth the church.

verses.restored: I wish all of you to speak in tongues, but more that you prophesy; greater is the one prophesying than the one speaking in tongues, unless one interprets, so that the assembly may receive building.

familiar.text: I would that ye all spake with tongues, but rather that ye prophesied: for greater is he that prophesieth than he that speaketh with tongues, except he interpret, that the church may receive edifying.

verses.restored: Now, siblings, if I come to you speaking in tongues, what will I benefit you unless I speak to you in revelation, knowledge, prophecy, or teaching?

familiar.text: Now, brethren, if I come unto you speaking with tongues, what shall I profit you, except I shall speak to you either by revelation, or by knowledge, or by prophesying, or by doctrine?

verses.restored: Even lifeless things giving sound, whether flute or lyre, if they do not give distinction in notes, how will what is played be known?

familiar.text: And even things without life giving sound, whether pipe or harp, except they give a distinction in the sounds, how shall it be known what is piped or harped?

verses.restored: For if a trumpet gives an unclear sound, who will prepare for battle?

familiar.text: For if the trumpet give an uncertain sound, who shall prepare himself to the battle?

verses.restored: So also you, unless through the tongue you give a clear word, how will what is spoken be known? For you will be speaking into air.

familiar.text: So likewise ye, except ye utter by the tongue words easy to be understood, how shall it be known what is spoken? for ye shall speak into the air.

verses.restored: There are perhaps so many kinds of voices in the world, and none is voiceless.

familiar.text: There are, it may be, so many kinds of voices in the world, and none of them is without signification.

verses.restored: If then I do not know the power/meaning of the voice, I will be a foreigner to the speaker and the speaker a foreigner to me.

familiar.text: Therefore if I know not the meaning of the voice, I shall be unto him that speaketh a barbarian, and he that speaketh shall be a barbarian unto me.

verses.restored: So also you, since you are zealous for spirits/spiritual things, seek that you may abound for building up the assembly.

familiar.text: Even so ye, forasmuch as ye are zealous of spiritual gifts, seek that ye may excel to the edifying of the church.

verses.restored: Therefore let the one speaking in a tongue pray that one may interpret.

familiar.text: Wherefore let him that speaketh in an unknown tongue pray that he may interpret.

verses.restored: For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays, but my mind is unfruitful.

familiar.text: For if I pray in an unknown tongue, my spirit prayeth, but my understanding is unfruitful.

verses.restored: What then is it? I will pray with the spirit, and I will also pray with the mind; I will sing praise with the spirit, and I will also sing praise with the mind.

familiar.text: What is it then? I will pray with the spirit, and I will pray with the understanding also: I will sing with the spirit, and I will sing with the understanding also.

verses.restored: Otherwise, if you bless in spirit, how will the one filling the place of the uninstructed say the Amen at your thanksgiving, since that one does not know what you say?

familiar.text: Else when thou shalt bless with the spirit, how shall he that occupieth the room of the unlearned say Amen at thy giving of thanks, seeing he understandeth not what thou sayest?

verses.restored: For you indeed give thanks beautifully/well, but the other is not built up.

familiar.text: For thou verily givest thanks well, but the other is not edified.

verses.restored: I thank the Divine, I speak in tongues more than all of you;

familiar.text: I thank my God, I speak with tongues more than ye all:

verses.restored: but in assembly I desire to speak five words with my mind, so that I may instruct others also, rather than ten thousand words in a tongue.

familiar.text: Yet in the church I had rather speak five words with my understanding, that by my voice I might teach others also, than ten thousand words in an unknown tongue.

verses.restored: Siblings, do not become children in thinking; in harmfulness be infants, but in thinking become mature/complete.

familiar.text: Brethren, be not children in understanding: howbeit in malice be ye children, but in understanding be men.

verses.restored: In the Law it has been written: By people of other tongues and by lips of others I will speak to this people, and not even thus will they hear me, says the Lord.

familiar.text: In the law it is written, With men of other tongues and other lips will I speak unto this people; and yet for all that will they not hear me, saith the LORD.

verses.restored: So then tongues are for a sign, not to those trusting but to the untrusting; but prophecy is not for the untrusting but for those trusting.

familiar.text: Wherefore tongues are for a sign, not to them that believe, but to them that believe not: but prophesying serveth not for them that believe not, but for them which believe.

verses.restored: If therefore the whole assembly comes together in the same place and all speak in tongues, and uninstructed or untrusting people enter, will they not say that you are mad?

familiar.text: If therefore the whole church be come together into one place, and all speak with tongues, and there come in those that are unlearned, or unbelievers, will they not say that ye are mad?

verses.restored: But if all prophesy, and some untrusting or uninstructed one enters, one is exposed by all, examined by all.

familiar.text: But if all prophesy, and there come in one that believeth not, or one unlearned, he is convinced of all, he is judged of all:

verses.restored: The hidden things of one's heart become manifest, and so falling on the face, one will worship the Divine, declaring that the Divine is truly among you.

familiar.text: And thus are the secrets of his heart made manifest; and so falling down on his face he will worship God, and report that God is in you of a truth.

verses.restored: What then is it, siblings? When you come together, each has a psalm, teaching, revelation, tongue, interpretation. Let all things happen for building up.

familiar.text: How is it then, brethren? when ye come together, every one of you hath a psalm, hath a doctrine, hath a tongue, hath a revelation, hath an interpretation. Let all things be done unto edifying.

verses.restored: If anyone speaks in a tongue, let it be by two or at most three, and each in turn, and let one interpret.

familiar.text: If any man speak in an unknown tongue, let it be by two, or at the most by three, and that by course; and let one interpret.

verses.restored: But if there is no interpreter, let one be silent in assembly, and speak to oneself and to the Divine.

familiar.text: But if there be no interpreter, let him keep silence in the church; and let him speak to himself, and to God.

verses.restored: Let two or three prophets speak, and let the others discern.

familiar.text: Let the prophets speak two or three, and let the other judge.

verses.restored: But if something is unveiled to another sitting by, let the first be silent.

familiar.text: If any thing be revealed to another that sitteth by, let the first hold his peace.

verses.restored: For you are all able to prophesy one by one, so that all may learn and all may be encouraged.

familiar.text: For ye may all prophesy one by one, that all may learn, and all may be comforted.

verses.restored: And spirits of prophets are subject to prophets.

familiar.text: And the spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets.

verses.restored: For the Divine is not of disorder but of peace. As in all the assemblies of the holy ones,

familiar.text: For God is not the author of confusion, but of peace, as in all churches of the saints.

verses.restored: let the women be silent in the assemblies, for it is not permitted to them to speak, but let them be subject, just as also the Law says.

familiar.text: Let your women keep silence in the churches: for it is not permitted unto them to speak; but they are commanded to be under obedience, as also saith the law.

verses.restored: But if they want to learn anything, let them ask their own husbands at home, for it is shameful for a woman to speak in assembly.

familiar.text: And if they will learn any thing, let them ask their husbands at home: for it is a shame for women to speak in the church.

verses.restored: Or did the word of the Divine go out from you? Or did it arrive to you only?

familiar.text: What? came the word of God out from you? or came it unto you only?

verses.restored: If anyone thinks oneself to be prophet or spiritual, let one recognize that what I write to you is a command of the Lord.

familiar.text: If any man think himself to be a prophet, or spiritual, let him acknowledge that the things that I write unto you are the commandments of the Lord.

verses.restored: But if anyone is ignorant, let that one be ignorant.

familiar.text: But if any man be ignorant, let him be ignorant.

verses.restored: So then, my siblings, desire to prophesy, and do not forbid speaking in tongues.

familiar.text: Wherefore, brethren, covet to prophesy, and forbid not to speak with tongues.

verses.restored: But let all things happen beautifully/well and according to order.

familiar.text: Let all things be done decently and in order.

translation_notes: Chapter 14 continues the chapter 13 love-rule: gifts are evaluated by whether they build the assembly.

Verses 34-35 must be read with caution alongside 1 Corinthians 11 where women pray and prophesy. Interpretive options include local disruption, quoted Corinthian slogan, or later interpolation; restored layer preserves the text while noting tension.
